findings.description: The ordinary local no-mistakes test command replaces run_full() with run_local_required(). The old run_full() called "$ROOT/tests/run.sh" with no arguments, admitting the complete behavior-test inventory through the sealed boundary. The new run_local_required() calls "$ROOT/tests/run.sh" "${herdr_tests[@]}", where herdr_tests is built by filtering tests/test-capabilities.tsv to only herdr-lab and herdr-mixed entries (line 63: 'herdr-lab|herdr-mixed) herdr_tests+=(...)'). Every hermetic-only behavior test file is omitted from local pre-push validation. The .no-mistakes.yaml comment at line 22 explicitly acknowledges this: 'It deliberately does not duplicate hermetic-only behavior files on the Mac.' The PR's own review flagged this as an error: 'Restore the complete local suite, or obtain explicit approval for this material weakening of the gate contract.' No explicit approval was obtained, and the intent stated 'instead of hiding the seven shallow-history failures behind new skips,' meaning the seven failures should have been fixed rather than the tests removed from local execution. The PR did fix the shallow-history root cause by changing --depth=1 fetches to full fetches in fm-azure-runner-guest.sh, but then removed the hermetic-only tests from local validation instead of verifying they now pass. This materially weakens the gate contract: a developer can push code that fails hermetic behavior tests without any local check catching it, relying solely on CI.

runs.summary: Reviewed the full diff for PR 327 (fix: enable detached Azure gate execution). The PR adds a private-direct-bundle mode for detached HEAD Azure routing, an offline Agent Fleet installer, full-history git fetches replacing shallow fetches, watcher subprocess cleanup via fm_super_stop_watcher, and a liveness test barrier mechanism. The Azure runner changes (private-direct-bundle mode, create_private_snapshot_from_head, verify_self_contained_private_bundle, Agent Fleet installer, four-name host-capability declaration, guest.sh full-history fetches with shallow-repository check) are structurally sound and well-tested. The watcher cleanup function fm_super_stop_watcher correctly terminates children before the watcher to prevent orphaning. However, the PR introduces one blocking finding: bin/fm-no-mistakes-test-command.sh replaces run_full() with run_local_required(), which only passes herdr-lab and herdr-mixed files to tests/run.sh, omitting every hermetic-only behavior test from local pre-push validation. The PR's own review flagged this as an error requiring restoration of the complete suite or explicit approval, but neither was provided. The intent explicitly stated the seven shallow-history failures should be fixed 'instead of hiding them behind new skips,' yet the PR removed the tests from local execution entirely. While the PR did fix the root cause (changing --depth=1 to full fetches), it did not verify the hermetic-only tests now pass locally before removing them. One suspicion is also raised about the liveness test's new barrier mechanism using FM_NM_TEST_BARRIER_DIR and FM_NM_TEST_BARRIER_PHASE environment variables whose support in the probe code cannot be verified from the diff.

suspicions.description: The liveness test (j1 case) now drives a post-baseline membership change through FM_NM_TEST_BARRIER_DIR and FM_NM_TEST_BARRIER_PHASE=before-progress-sample environment variables passed to the probe ($PROBE). The probe must support these barrier variables to block at the specified phase, release on a barrier file write, and then complete its sample. The probe implementation is not in the diff, so it cannot be verified from the packet alone that these variables are actually handled. If the probe does not support the barrier mechanism, the test would hang at wait_for_barrier and eventually fail, or the probe might ignore the variables and produce an incorrect verdict. The old approach relied on sleep 0.2 turnover timing which was flaky under load; the new barrier approach is more deterministic but depends on unverified probe support.

runs.summary: Reviewed the full diff between base 4165bf07952aa198c2b2959d1aa8f19940bf39bb and head 3c8c480efeceadfdf56e11e48f8c7d101b02ec2b. This PR adds a direct private-bundle Azure route for detached no-mistakes gate HEADs, an offline Agent Fleet installer, non-shallow guest fetches, watcher subprocess cleanup, and liveness test barrier instrumentation. The Azure runner changes (private-direct-bundle mode, bundle creation/verification, retry handling, Agent Fleet installer) appear structurally sound with proper fail-closed checks. Two suspicions are raised: (1) the liveness test relies on FM_NM_TEST_BARRIER_DIR/FM_NM_TEST_BARRIER_PHASE hooks whose probe implementation is not visible in this diff, and (2) the PR's own review flagged potential weakening of local pre-push behavior coverage that remains unresolved. The existing blocking finding cc-8f48584d092b cannot be verified as fixed from this diff alone and remains open.

suspicions.description: The rewritten one-shot liveness test (j1) passes FM_NM_TEST_BARRIER_DIR and FM_NM_TEST_BARRIER_PHASE environment variables to the probe ($PROBE), expecting it to pause at a 'before-progress-sample' barrier until a release file is written. However, no changes to the probe implementation (likely bin/fm-nm-step-liveness.sh or similar) appear in this diff. If the probe does not already support these barrier hooks, the test would complete immediately without waiting for the barrier, the successor process would not be present during the sample window, and the 'alive' verdict would not be produced — causing the test to fail. The PR claims this test passed, which implies the hooks pre-exist, but this cannot be confirmed from the diff alone. If the hooks are absent, the test is non-functional and the liveness positive signal is unverified.

The PR's own review step flagged that the ordinary/local no-mistakes path now passes only herdr-lab and herdr-mixed files to tests/run.sh, omitting every hermetic-only behavior test before push. The PR risk assessment rates this 'High' and acknowledges it lacks authorization in the stated intent. While docs/configuration.md describes the coverage contract as the union of local Herdr host set and CI executed-manifest, the review explicitly required either restoring the complete local suite or obtaining explicit approval for this material weakening of the gate contract. Neither resolution is visible in the final diff. The local test parallelization (run_local_required) does not change which files are run — the herdr_tests derivation appears unchanged — but the concern about the overall coverage posture remains unaddressed in this PR.
